requirements.title: A nonempty whole array name aligns like its first element
requirements.definition: For a nonzero-sized array used as an equivalence object, its unqualified name has the effect of a designator for the first element in array element order. The first element is determined by actual bounds, not by blindly substituting index1 in every dimension. This rule does not supply a nonexistent first element for an empty array or make the whole array scalar.

pending.default-lower-bound: PENDING future complete parent: INTEGER a(2),s; EQUIVALENCE (a,s). Define a(1)=11,a(2)=17; check s==11. Then s=23; check a(1)==23,a(2)==17. Use direct coordinates and literals, reached-check counts and complete defined states.
pending.nonunit-lower-bound: PENDING future parent: INTEGER a(-1:1),s; whole-name set (a,s). Define a(-1)=3,a(0)=7,a(1)=11; check s==3. Set s=13 and check only a(-1) changed while a(0),a(1) retain7,11. The first element is a(-1), not a(1).
pending.rank-two-first-element: PENDING future parent: INTEGER a(0:1,3:4),s; set (a,s). Explicitly define all four coordinates to3,7,11,13 in Table9.1 order. Check s==3, then s=17 and check a(0,3)==17 with every other element unchanged. No RESHAPE, loop-generated oracle or numerical address difference supplies the expected mapping.
